wallbox.title: Wallbox
wallbox.description: Surplus charging for electric vehicles plus an optional separate wallbox consumption meter. This removes EV charging peaks from the house consumption so that optimizer/forecast/EWMA remain stable.

data.wallbox_included_in_house: House consumption meter already includes the wallbox (e.g. openWB on the utility meter)

evcc.title: EVCC integration
evcc.description:
Connects Maestro to EVCC, openWB or any other wallbox controller. Maestro steps back as soon as the configured charge mode sensor reports the 'instant charging' value – the wallbox can then use the grid.

Works with any wallbox that provides a sensor or select entity which reports a defined value in 'instant charging' (or similar) mode:
• EVCC: sensor with value "now"
• openWB: sensor with value "Instant Charging"
• Other wallboxes: any sensor/select, as long as the instant charging value is known.

data.evcc_charging_entity: Charging active entity (optional, boolean/binary_sensor – e.g. openWB autoladestatus)
data.evcc_mode_entity: Charge mode entity (sensor/select with instant charging value – e.g. EVCC, openWB, others)

heatpump.title: Heat pump
heatpump.description: Control the heat pump on PV surplus or cheap electricity.

auto_mode.title: F3: Auto-optimization
auto_mode.description: Optimizes the F0 parameters daily according to the selected objective. Requires ≥7 days of consumption + PV history. Manual inputs immediately override the auto override.

sizing_advisor.title: Battery & PV Sizing Advisor
sizing_advisor.description: Map the long-term statistics sensors from the HA Energy Dashboard. The simulation calculates how much grid import could have been avoided with more battery or PV capacity.

data.sizing_house_from_balance: Derive house load from energy balance (ignore house consumption sensor)
data.sizing_import_from_energy_dashboard: Re-import sensors from HA Energy Dashboard (overwrites saved values)

dashboard.title: Add dashboard
dashboard.description:
Setup is complete.

**Classic dashboard:**
1. **Hard-reload** the browser (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R)
2. **Settings → Dashboards → Add dashboard**
3. Under **Community dashboards**, select **E3DC Maestro**
4. Confirm the title **E3DC Maestro**

Requirements: Home Assistant ≥ 2026.5 plus Mushroom Cards and ApexCharts Card from HACS.

The URL path must be `e3dc-maestro` for the help links to work. On older HA versions the dashboard can still be imported manually as YAML.

data_description.grid_power_sensor: Recommended: _transfer_to_from_grid (signed, then enable 'Invert' below). Alternatively _export_to_grid (feed-in only, grid import will be missing!).
data_description.grid_power_invert: Enable if the sensor reports positive = grid import (applies to _transfer_to_from_grid). Maestro convention: positive = feed-in.

system.title: System parameters

data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Enter the usable (net) capacity. The auto-detected value above is the gross capacity from the RSCP diagnostics and should NOT be copied 1:1.
data_description.advanced_corridor: Enables separate upper/lower limits for the charge corridor. Disabled: Maestro uses symmetric default values.
data_description.lower_corridor: Minimum charge power in corridor mode (W). If the surplus falls below this value, Maestro does not charge.
data_description.upper_corridor: Maximum charge power in corridor mode (W). Surplus above this is fed into the grid (unless the feed-in limit is reached).
data_description.soc_hysteresis_percent: Prevents constant on/off switching at SoC thresholds. Maestro only switches again once the SoC has moved above/below the threshold by this amount.
data_description.charge_ramp_w_per_cycle: Charge power is ramped up by this amount per cycle instead of jumping straight to maximum. Reduces inverter stress.
data_description.update_interval: Interval in seconds at which Maestro reads new data and makes a control decision. Default 30 s.

season.title: Season & charge corridor
season.description: Defines the charge target and the emergency charge threshold. The seasonal reserve always keeps a minimum SoC as backup for power outages; the adaptive reserve learns from actual night-time consumption.

data.charge_threshold: Charge threshold – emergency charge below x% SoC

data_description.charge_threshold: Below this SoC, Maestro recharges immediately, regardless of PV or tariff (emergency protection).
data_description.charge_target: Maximum charge SoC in normal operation. Values >95 % accelerate cell aging.
data_description.winter_minimum_hour: Until this hour (e.g. 7 = 07:00), Maestro ensures in winter that the battery is fully charged for the morning.
data_description.summer_charge_end: Target time for the end of charging in summer – after that, only PV surplus is used for recharging.
data_description.reserve_winter_percent: Fixed minimum reserve in winter (Dec–Feb) for power outages.
data_description.reserve_equinox_percent: Reserve at the equinox (Mar/Sep) – transitional value between winter and summer.
data_description.adaptive_reserve_safety_factor: Multiplier applied to the calculated night-time demand (e.g. 1.2 = 20 % buffer). Higher values = more reserve, but less depth of discharge.
data_description.adaptive_reserve_lookback_days: How many past days are used for averaging consumption.
data_description.adaptive_reserve_min_days: Minimum number of data points – below this, the static seasonal reserve applies instead of the adaptive one.
data_description.adaptive_reserve_max_soc: Upper limit for the adaptive reserve. Prevents the battery from permanently staying at a high SoC.

pv_forecast.title: PV forecast / charge delay
pv_forecast.description: Forecast sensors for today and tomorrow. Forward-Looking and the auto-optimizer (48 h horizon) use the tomorrow forecast. For the hourly profile of the following day, configure the same Solcast "Forecast tomorrow" sensor (with detailedHourly).

data.pv_forecast_sensor: Forecast today – remaining kWh (e.g. Solcast: Forecast remaining today)
data.tomorrow_pv_sensor: Forecast tomorrow – daily total kWh (e.g. Solcast: Forecast tomorrow) – Forward-Looking and fallback for 48 h optimizer
data.pv_forecast_sensor_day2: Forecast tomorrow (hourly profile) – optional (e.g. Solcast: Forecast tomorrow) – enables 48 h horizon in the auto-optimizer
data.forward_looking_enabled: Enable Forward-Looking (charges ahead when little PV is expected tomorrow)
data.low_yield_priority_enabled: Low-yield PV day: enable battery priority
data.pv_forecast_today_sensor: Forecast today – daily total kWh (e.g. Solcast: Forecast today) – for low-yield PV day

data_description.pv_forecast_safety_factor: The forecast must reach at least (demand × factor) for charging to be delayed. E.g. 1.2 = 20 % safety buffer.
data_description.pv_forecast_threshold_kwh: Absolute lower limit: if the forecast is below this, charging is never delayed (e.g. 1.0 kWh for a small system).
data_description.delay_min_soc: If the battery is below this SoC, charging is never delayed – regardless of the forecast.
data_description.spreading_target_soc: Charge spreading distributes charging evenly until the seasonal charge end (charge_end). The target SoC is the upper limit – above it, charging is actively blocked so that PV surplus flows into the grid.
data_description.forward_looking_max_soc: Maximum SoC to which Maestro pre-charges when the tomorrow forecast is poor. Values >90 % accelerate cell aging.
data_description.low_yield_threshold: Ratio of daily forecast ÷ reference below which Maestro activates battery priority (e.g. 0.5 = half as sunny as a reference day).
data_description.low_yield_reference_kwh: Optional manual reference value. 0 means: automatic from installed kWp × factor and PV statistics.
data_description.low_yield_reference_kwh_per_kwp: Factor for the kWp baseline: default 5.5 kWh/kWp corresponds to a very sunny summer day.

ht.title: HT/NT protection
ht.description: Prevents discharging during the high-tariff window and keeps a SoC reserve for expensive periods.

data_description.ht_on: Integer in local time, e.g. 7 for 07:00.
data_description.ht_off: Integer in local time, e.g. 21 for 21:00.
data_description.ht_min: Target SoC that Maestro keeps at minimum during the high-tariff window (winter, Dec–Feb).
data_description.ht_sockel: Reserve at the equinox – transitional value between winter and summer.

data_description.class_: high = battery covers the house down to the reserve, below that discharge block · low = cheap window (optional active grid charging) · normal = neutral.
data_description.min_reserve_soc: Maestro keeps at least this SoC during the slot. Leave empty for no reserve requirement.

tariff.title: Tariff & costs
tariff.description: Electricity tariff mode and €/kWh prices. With a fixed tariff, Maestro blocks strategies that would charge the battery from the grid.

data.low_slot_grid_charge_enabled: Active grid charging in low slot
data.low_slot_target_soc: Grid charge target in low slot (% SoC)

data_description.battery_capex_eur: Purchase price of the battery in €. Used for the wear cost calculation (cell wear per kWh).
data_description.battery_total_cycles: Lifetime full cycles according to the manufacturer's datasheet (e.g. 6000 for LFP). Determines the wear cost per cycle.
data_description.cheap_threshold: If the spot price is below this, Maestro allows charging from the grid (up to max_grid_charge_kwh per day).
data_description.max_grid_charge_kwh: Maximum grid charging energy per calendar day. Prevents daily full charging from the grid.
data_description.low_slot_grid_charge_enabled: Actively charges from the grid during a low slot until the target SoC is reached – regardless of the tariff mode. Useful for classic NT windows to bridge the time until PV coverage. Limited by the daily budget above.
data_description.low_slot_target_soc: Target SoC up to which the battery is charged from the grid during the low slot. With forecast-based amount, this value acts as the upper limit.
data_description.low_slot_forecast_based: Instead of a fixed target SoC, only as much is recharged as is needed according to tomorrow's PV/consumption forecast (requires the sensors for forecast tomorrow + consumption tomorrow). The target SoC above then acts as the upper limit. If forecast data is missing, the fixed target SoC applies.
data_description.price_plan_enabled: Uses the price curve (price sensor with raw_today/raw_tomorrow or similar) to compute when grid charging and a discharge hold pay off. Display only for now (sensor "Price plan") – nothing is controlled.
data_description.price_plan_max_soc: The price plan charges at most up to this SoC.
data_description.price_plan_min_spread: Grid charging is only planned if the expected price advantage after losses is at least this large.
data_description.price_plan_efficiency: Share of charged energy that can be discharged later (typically 0.85–0.92).
data_description.price_plan_safety_factor: Factor on the forecast house consumption (1.15 = 15 % margin) so expensive slots are safely covered from the battery.

wallbox.title: Wallbox
wallbox.description: Surplus charging for electric vehicles. The optional wallbox power sensor removes EV charging peaks from the house consumption so that optimizer and forecast remain stable.

data.wallbox_included_in_house: Wallbox already included in house consumption meter

data_description.wallbox_min_surplus: Maestro only starts the wallbox once this PV surplus is consistently available (hysteresis prevents cycling).
data_description.wallbox_min_current: Minimum charging current per IEC 61851 (normally 6 A). Below this, Maestro prefers to switch the wallbox off.
data_description.wallbox_included_in_house: Enable for openWB on the utility meter or if the house consumption sensor already counts the wallbox. Prevents double counting.

evcc.title: EVCC integration
evcc.description:
Connects Maestro to EVCC, openWB or any other wallbox controller. Maestro steps back as soon as the configured charge mode sensor reports the 'instant charging' value.

Supported systems:
• EVCC: sensor with value "now"
• openWB: sensor with value "Instant Charging"
• Other wallboxes: any sensor/select that reports a known value during instant charging.

data.evcc_mode_entity: Charge mode entity (sensor/select with instant charging value)

data_description.evcc_discharge_limit_w: Maximum battery discharge power while EVCC is in instant charging mode. 0 = discharging completely blocked.

heatpump.title: Heat pump
heatpump.description: Controls the heat pump on PV surplus or when the electricity price falls below the price limit.

data_description.hp_min_surplus: Maestro only switches the heat pump on once this PV surplus is exceeded.
data_description.hp_max_price: Even with little PV, the heat pump can switch on if the spot price is below this. 0 = PV surplus only.
data_description.hp_min_run_minutes: Minimum run time after switching on. Prevents short cycling that stresses the compressor.
data_description.hp_min_pause_minutes: Minimum pause after switching off. Protects against restarting too quickly.

data_description.watchdog_timeout: If Maestro makes no control decision for longer than this value (e.g. HA crash or sensor failure), it resets the E3DC inverter to a safe idle state. 0 = disabled.

data_description.morning_cap_soc: Until the specified time, Maestro does not let the battery rise above this SoC – leaving room for midday PV.
data_description.morning_cap_until_h: After this hour (local time), Maestro lifts the SoC cap.
data_description.gentle_charge_factor: Share of max. charge power used for gentle charging (0.05 = 5 %, 1.0 = full power). Lower values are gentler on the cells but slow down charging.

auto_mode.title: F3: Auto-optimization
auto_mode.description: Optimizes the F0 parameters daily according to the selected objective. Requires at least 7 days of consumption and PV history.

data_description.auto_mode_objective: self_consumption = maximum self-consumption rate · cost = minimum electricity costs (requires price sensor) · co2 = minimum CO₂ emissions.

sizing_advisor.description: Map the long-term statistics sensors from the HA Energy Dashboard. The simulation calculates how much grid import could have been avoided with more battery or PV capacity.

data.sizing_import_from_energy_dashboard: Re-import sensors from HA Energy Dashboard (overwrites saved values)
